sources.entry: pydantic - Data validation using Python type hints.

summary.one_liner: Pydantic is a Python library for data validation and parsing that uses standard type hints to define and check data structures.
summary.what_it_does: Lets you define data models as Python classes that subclass BaseModel, with fields annotated by type hints. When you construct a model from input data, Pydantic validates and coerces values to the declared types, for example converting the string '123' to an int or a date string to a datetime. Invalid input raises an error. The README shows a simple User model that parses a dict with mixed-type values into typed attributes. Pydantic V2 is described as a ground-up rewrite with performance improvements; V2 also bundles the V1.10 code under pydantic.v1 for incremental migration. Installation is via pip or conda-forge.
use_cases: validate API request or response data
parse untyped JSON or dict input into typed objects
migrate a codebase from Pydantic V1 to V2
define typed configuration or data schemas
coerce string inputs to ints, dates and lists
how_to_run: from pydantic import BaseModel; define a class subclassing BaseModel with typed fields
User(**data) to validate and construct an instance
notable: Validation driven by standard Python type hints rather than a custom schema language
Coerces compatible input types, e.g. '123' to int and date strings to datetime
Pydantic V2 ships the V1.10 API as pydantic.v1 for incremental upgrades
Works with linters and IDEs because models are plain Python classes
caveats: Requires Python 3.10 or newer according to the README
The README points to separate V1.10 documentation and a 1.10.X-fixes branch for V1 users, so V1 and V2 behavior differ
Performance tuning options are described only in the external installation docs
